title: Organic Molecules
standard_text: Organic molecular structures: functional groups, homologous series (alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, haloalkanes, alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters); IUPAC naming and formulae; structural isomers; physical properties and intermolecular forces; reactions: combustion, esterification, substitution, addition and elimination; plastics and polymers. (summary of the senior secondary Chemistry curriculum, SSS 3; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 Chemistry worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): naming hydrocarbons, functional groups, alcohols, aldehydes and ketones, acids, esters and amines and isomers, reactions and polymers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A homologous series has the same functional group and general formula.
body_html:
How to think about it

Organic compounds contain carbon. Each homologous series has a functional group: C=C (alkenes), –OH (alcohols), –CHO (aldehydes), C=O in the chain (ketones), –COOH (carboxylic acids), –COO– (esters). IUPAC names use the longest chain (meth-, eth-, prop-, but-, pent-) and the suffix of the functional group.

Boiling points increase with chain length (stronger intermolecular forces) and are higher for alcohols and acids (hydrogen bonds). Alkanes undergo substitution with halogens; alkenes undergo addition (hydrogenation, hydration, halogenation); elimination makes alkenes. An alcohol and a carboxylic acid form an ester. Addition polymers such as polythene are made from alkenes.

Example

Name CH₃CH₂CH₂OH.

3 carbons, –OH on C1

Answer: propan-1-ol

Example

Ethanol + ethanoic acid → ?

Esterification

Answer: ethyl ethanoate + water

Common mistakes

  • Numbering the chain from the wrong end.
  • Thinking alkenes undergo substitution.
  • Mixing up aldehydes and ketones.

faq.q: Why does butane boil at a higher temperature than propane?
faq.a: It is a longer molecule with stronger intermolecular forces.

faq.q: Why are plastics a problem for the environment?
faq.a: Most are not biodegradable, so they last for hundreds of years in landfills and oceans.

items.q: Which compound has the formula C₄H₉OH?
items.e: Count the carbon atoms (4: but-) and look at the functional group.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkane with 3 carbon atoms?
items.e: Alkanes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which alkane forms when 1-bromobutane reacts with sodium in dry ether (Wurtz reaction)?
items.e: Two alkyl groups join: 2R–X + 2Na → R–R. A C4 group gives octane.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of propane?
items.e: Propane has 3 carbon atoms (prop-). Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH=CHCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 6 carbons (hex-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 6 carbons (hex-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of ethene?
items.e: Ethene has 2 carbon atoms (eth-). Alkenes are CₙH₂ₙ.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkane with 19 carbon atoms?
items.e: Alkanes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkane with 6 carbon atoms?
items.e: Alkanes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of butene?
items.e: Butene has 4 carbon atoms (but-). Alkenes are CₙH₂ₙ.

items.q: Which alkane forms when 1-bromopropane reacts with sodium in dry ether (Wurtz reaction)?
items.e: Two alkyl groups join: 2R–X + 2Na → R–R. A C3 group gives hexane.

items.q: Which compound has the formula C₄H₁₀?
items.e: Count the carbon atoms (4: but-) and look at the functional group.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 3 carbons (prop-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>=CHCH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 3 carbons (prop-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which alkane forms when bromoethane reacts with sodium in dry ether (Wurtz reaction)?
items.e: Two alkyl groups join: 2R–X + 2Na → R–R. A C2 group gives butane.

items.q: Which compound has the formula C₄H₈?
items.e: Count the carbon atoms (4: but-) and look at the functional group.

items.q: Which alkane forms when bromomethane reacts with sodium in dry ether (Wurtz reaction)?
items.e: Two alkyl groups join: 2R–X + 2Na → R–R. A C1 group gives ethane.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkane with 16 carbon atoms?
items.e: Alkanes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>.

items.q: Which class of compound has the functional group –CHO?
items.e: –CHO is the functional group of an aldehyde.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH=CHCH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 6 carbons (hex-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which functional group is found in a carboxylic acid?
items.e: –COOH is the functional group of a carboxylic acid.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>=CHCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>Cl?
items.e: The longest chain has 3 carbons (prop-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>Br?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>=CHCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(OH)CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which functional group is found in an amide?
items.e: –CONH₂ is the functional group of an amide.

items.q: Which functional group is found in an amine?
items.e: –NH₂ is the functional group of an amine.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkane with 20 carbon atoms?
items.e: Alkanes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>.

items.q: Which functional group is found in an ether?
items.e: –O– (between two carbons) is the functional group of an ether.

items.q: Which class of compound has the functional group –NH₂?
items.e: –NH₂ is the functional group of an amine.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>BrCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 3 carbons (prop-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>OHCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which functional group is found in an alcohol?
items.e: –OH (on an alkyl group) is the functional group of an alcohol.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>ClCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 3 carbons (prop-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which class of compound has the functional group –NO₂?
items.e: –NO₂ is the functional group of a nitro compound.

items.q: Which is the strongest base?
items.e: The alkyl group pushes electrons onto the nitrogen lone pair.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from methanoic acid and pentan-1-ol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (pentyl), then the acid part (methanoate).

items.q: What is used to give a coloured spot for amino acids in chromatography?
items.e: Amino acids are colourless.

items.q: Why does the product of HCN adding to ethanal form a racemic mixture?
c: CN⁻ can attack the planar carbonyl from either side equally
the product has no chiral carbon
items.e: Equal amounts of both enantiomers form.

items.q: What is a racemic mixture?
c: a mixture of E and Z isomers
equal amounts of two enantiomers, so it does not rotate plane-polarised light
items.e: The rotations cancel.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from methanoic acid and propan-1-ol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (propyl), then the acid part (methanoate).

items.q: Butyl propanoate is hydrolysed. Which acid and alcohol form?
items.e: Split at the C–O bond: the -oate part gives the acid, the -yl part gives the alcohol.

items.q: What is the product when an acyl chloride reacts with water?
items.e: Nucleophilic addition–elimination.

items.q: Which reagent reduces a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol?
items.e: NaBH₄ does not reduce acids.

items.q: What is the product when ethanoyl chloride reacts with ammonia?
items.e: Addition–elimination gives an amide.

items.q: Butyl ethanoate is hydrolysed. Which acid and alcohol form?
items.e: Split at the C–O bond: the -oate part gives the acid, the -yl part gives the alcohol.

items.q: What is decarboxylation?
c: removal of CO₂ from a carboxylic acid salt, often with soda lime
items.e: Sodium ethanoate gives methane.

items.q: Why is phenylamine a weaker base than ethylamine?
c: the nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring
items.e: The lone pair is less available to accept a proton.

items.q: What type of polymer is Terylene (PET)?
items.e: Made from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid.

items.q: What does 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH) detect?
items.e: Both aldehydes and ketones react.

items.q: What is formed when an aldehyde reacts with hydroxylamine?
items.e: C=N–OH.

items.q: What gas forms when a carboxylic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?
items.e: This fizzing is a test for carboxylic acids.

items.q: Which compound gives a red precipitate when warmed with Fehling's solution?
items.e: Aldehydes reduce Cu²⁺ to Cu₂O.

items.q: Methyl ethanoate is hydrolysed. Which acid and alcohol form?
items.e: Split at the C–O bond: the -oate part gives the acid, the -yl part gives the alcohol.

items.q: What type of isomerism do amino acids (except glycine) show?
items.e: They have a chiral carbon.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkane with 17 carbon atoms?
items.e: Alkanes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>.

items.q: What is the major product when HBr adds to propene?
items.e: It goes via the more stable secondary carbocation.

items.q: How many structural isomers does C₄H₁₀ have?
items.e: Butane and methylpropane.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from ethanoic acid and pentan-1-ol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (pentyl), then the acid part (ethanoate).

items.q: How do catalytic converters remove carbon monoxide and NO?
items.e: A platinum or rhodium catalyst is used.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from ethanoic acid and butan-1-ol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (butyl), then the acid part (ethanoate).

items.q: Which reagent replaces the diazonium group with hydrogen?
items.e: This gives benzene.

items.q: What colour is the azo dye formed from benzenediazonium chloride and phenol?
items.e: p-Hydroxyazobenzene.

items.q: What is an addition polymer?
c: a long chain made by joining many alkene monomers, with no other product
a chain that forms with water as a by-product
items.e: Polyethene comes from ethene.

items.q: Which step of free-radical substitution removes radicals?
items.e: Two radicals join, for example Cl• + Cl• → Cl₂.

items.q: What type of bond joins amino acids in a protein?
items.e: Water is released in a condensation reaction.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What are structural isomers?
c: compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae
atoms of the same element with different neutrons
items.e: Butane and methylpropane are isomers.

items.q: Why are biodegradable polymers such as polylactic acid useful?
c: they are made from crude oil only
microorganisms can break them down, reducing plastic waste
items.e: PLA is made from plant starch.

items.q: What is made when an alcohol is dehydrated with hot concentrated phosphoric acid?
items.e: Water is eliminated.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>ClCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Why is the C–I bond the most reactive carbon–halogen bond?
c: it has the lowest bond enthalpy
items.e: Bond strength matters more than polarity.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from pentanoic acid and methanol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (methyl), then the acid part (pentanoate).

items.q: How many moles of oxygen are needed to burn one mole of C<sub>10</sub>H<sub>22</sub> completely?
items.e: C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub> + (3n+1)/2 O<sub>2</sub> → nCO<sub>2</sub> + (n+1)H<sub>2</sub>O. 10 CO₂ need 20 O atoms, 11 H₂O need 11 O atoms: 31 ÷ 2 = 15½.

items.q: Which ester is made when ethanoic acid reacts with butanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (butyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: Which ester is made when propanoic acid reacts with propanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (propyl) and the acid gives the second part (propanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: How many moles of oxygen are needed to burn one mole of C<sub>15</sub>H<sub>32</sub> completely?
items.e: C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub> + (3n+1)/2 O<sub>2</sub> → nCO<sub>2</sub> + (n+1)H<sub>2</sub>O. 15 CO₂ need 30 O atoms, 16 H₂O need 16 O atoms: 46 ÷ 2 = 23.

items.q: Which polymer is used for water pipes and cable insulation?
items.e: Poly(chloroethene) (PVC): water pipes and cable insulation.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>Cl?
items.e: The longest chain has 6 carbons (hex-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>OHCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 6 carbons (hex-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH)CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 3 carbons (prop-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which two compounds react to make ethyl propanoate?
items.e: Ethyl- comes from ethanol; -propanoate comes from propanoic acid.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkane with 4 carbon atoms?
items.e: Alkanes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the monomer of poly(tetrafluoroethene) (PTFE)?
items.e: Remove “poly” and the brackets to find the monomer.

items.q: Which group shows a +I effect?
items.e: Alkyl groups release electrons.

items.q: Which ester is made when ethanoic acid reacts with propanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (propyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: What forms when bromoethane is heated with ethanolic KOH?
items.e: In ethanol, OH⁻ acts as a base.

items.q: Which two compounds react to make propyl ethanoate?
items.e: Propyl- comes from propanol; -ethanoate comes from ethanoic acid.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(OH)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which ester is made when ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (ethyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkene with 17 carbon atoms and one C=C bond?
items.e: Alkenes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>.

items.q: Which monomer, chloroethene, is used to make an addition polymer? Choose its formula.
items.e: Every addition monomer has a C=C double bond.

items.q: How many moles of oxygen are needed to burn one mole of C<sub>16</sub>H<sub>34</sub> completely?
items.e: C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub> + (3n+1)/2 O<sub>2</sub> → nCO<sub>2</sub> + (n+1)H<sub>2</sub>O. 16 CO₂ need 32 O atoms, 17 H₂O need 17 O atoms: 49 ÷ 2 = 24½.
